title: Automate Security and Compliance
objective: Continuously govern human and machine permissions, secrets, configuration assessments, and audits.

sections.title: Separate Human and Machine Identities
paragraphs: In large-scale environments, distinguish human sign-ins, application execution roles, CI/CD deployment roles, and temporary credentials for external systems. Combine least privilege, federation, attribute-based access control, permissions boundaries, and organizational SCPs, and do not distribute broad, long-term credentials.

When investigating an access denial, review the effective permissions, including not only identity policies but also resource policies, session policies, permissions boundaries, SCPs, and explicit denies. Adding administrator permissions is not a substitute for investigating the cause.

sources.label: DOP-C02 Exam Guide: Large-Scale IAM Implementation

sections.title: Integrating Secrets and Data Protection into Delivery Pipelines
paragraphs: Do not embed secrets in source code, container images, templates, or logs. Design storage locations that only the principals requiring access at runtime can retrieve secrets from, along with rotation, encryption, auditing, and procedures for updating them during failures.

For data protection at rest and in transit, verify which principals can use the keys, backup and restoration procedures, whether sensitive values could enter logs, and cross-account sharing. Enabling encryption is not sufficient if decryption permissions or log-viewing permissions are too broad.

sources.label: DOP-C02 Exam Guide: Automating Data Protection

sections.title: Continuously Evaluating Configuration and Operational Audit Trails
paragraphs: An audit design links the target resources, expected configurations, evaluation rules, exceptions, expiration dates, change actors, and remediation results. By retaining not only current configurations but also configuration and operational histories, you can track when each change was made, by whom, and what was changed.

Automated remediation does not mean erasing audit findings. After remediation, reassess the desired state and verify that the same deviation does not recur. To avoid unconditionally overriding exceptions, incorporate approved exclusion scopes into the evaluation.

checkpoints.prompt: Ensure that the CI/CD deployment role can perform only stack updates in a specific account. Choose the single most appropriate permission design.

choices.text: Use administrator access keys shared by all pipelines.
choices.explanation: This sacrifices permission scope and auditability.

choices.text: Design a role limited to the update operations and resources in the target account, together with trust conditions and the required session conditions.
choices.explanation: This achieves least privilege for the machine identity and identifies the principal.

choices.text: Add permanent administrator permissions when access is denied.
choices.explanation: This violates least privilege without investigating the cause of the effective permissions.

checkpoints.prompt: We need to provide production database credentials securely to the application and update them regularly. Choose one most appropriate secret-management policy.

choices.text: Embed the credentials in the source code and container image.
choices.explanation: This creates risks of leakage and makes updates impossible.

choices.text: Do not verify the connection after rotation.
choices.explanation: The update could cause a service outage.

choices.text: Design secret storage with retrieval restricted by the execution role, along with rotation, encryption, auditing, and connection procedures for updates.
choices.explanation: This protects the secrets through both the delivery path and operational procedures.

checkpoints.prompt: An auditor wants to continuously detect unencrypted storage and remediate it except for approved exceptions. Choose one design for the most appropriate continuous control.

choices.text: Delete the audit results to reduce the number of detected findings to zero.
choices.explanation: This does not resolve the actual deviations.

choices.text: Evaluate the expected configuration and the expiration dates of exceptions, and combine configuration history, operation history, least-privilege remediation, and reevaluation.
choices.explanation: This enables continuous management of evidence, exceptions, and remediation results.

choices.text: Overwrite all storage unconditionally without checking for exceptions.
choices.explanation: This could damage approved configurations or operational procedures.
